fullPassage: Many of the parents we work with say things like, “I’ve tried everything. I’ve grounded him, taken away his Xbox, turned off the Internet, and made him quit the soccer team. I’ve got nothing left to take away.” When a kid repeatedly misbehaves, the temptation is to think, Well, they’ll never learn with a five-foot wall. Better make it ten feet. But Ross Greene, who is also a champion of collaborative problem-solving, points out that the kids who get the most negative consequences often learn the least from them. Years of research have shown that children can become self-disciplined, empathic, compassionate, and successful adults without painful punishment. So if they don’t seem to learn after a mild consequence, give them time. They might have to crash into that five-foot wall more than you’d like them to. Be patient. Express confidence that they’ll figure it out. They will.

questions.stem:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

Many of the parents we work with say things like, “I’ve tried everything. I’ve grounded him, taken away his Xbox, turned off the Internet, and made him quit the soccer team. I’ve got nothing left to take away.”

(A) But Ross Greene, who is also a champion of collaborative problem-solving, points out that the kids who get the most negative consequences often learn the least from them. Years of research have shown that children can become self-disciplined, empathic, compassionate, and successful adults without painful punishment.

(B) So if they don’t seem to learn after a mild consequence, give them time. They might have to crash into that five-foot wall more than you’d like them to. Be patient. Express confidence that they’ll figure it out. They will.

(C) When a kid repeatedly misbehaves, the temptation is to think, Well, they’ll never learn with a five-foot wall. Better make it ten feet.

det.analysis:
✅ ③ (C)→(A)→(B): 부모의 하소연 뒤 → (C) 아이가 반복해 잘못하면 벽을 높이고 싶은 유혹 → (A) But으로 그 유혹을 반박(처벌 많이 받은 아이가 덜 배움 + 연구) → (B) So로 결론(시간을 주고 인내하라)
❌ ① (A)→(C)→(B): (A)의 But이 반박할 대상(유혹)이 아직 없고, (A)의 연구 결론 뒤에 (C)의 처벌 강화 유혹이 오면 (B)의 So가 이어지지 못함
❌ ② (B)→(A)→(C): 결론(B)이 근거보다 먼저 나와 논리 역전
❌ ④ (C)→(B)→(A): (B)의 So(그러므로)가 받을 연구 근거(A)가 뒤에 있어 부자연스러움
det.tip: 유혹(C) → But 반박+연구(A) → So 결론(B)

✅ ① everything: 모든 것을 시도했다 — 적절

❌ ③ Be thankful(감사해라): 문맥과 무관
❌ ④ Be realistic(현실적이 되어라): 아이를 믿고 기다리라는 조언과 방향이 다름
det.tip: patient: 인내심 있는 — give them time과 호응

questions.passage: Many of the parents we work with say things like, “I’ve tried everything. I’ve grounded him, taken away his Xbox, turned off the Internet, and made him quit the soccer team. I’ve got nothing left to take away.” When a kid repeatedly misbehaves, the temptation is to think, Well, they’ll never learn with a five-foot wall. Better make it ten feet. But Ross Greene, who is also a champion of collaborative problem-solving, points out that the kids who get the most negative consequences often learn the least from them. Years of research have shown that children can become self-disciplined, empathic, compassionate, and successful adults without painful punishment. So if they don’t seem to learn after a mild consequence, give them time. They might have to crash into that five-foot wall more than you’d like them to. Be patient. Express confidence that they’ll figure it out. They will.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 요지: 처벌을 강화하기보다 아이가 가벼운 결과를 겪으며 스스로 배우도록 인내심 있게 기다려라
det.analysis:
❌ ① Children learn best when punishments become stronger each time.(처벌이 강해질수록 아이는 잘 배운다) — 글과 정반대
✅ ② Parents should wait patiently while children learn from mild consequences.(부모는 아이가 가벼운 결과에서 배우는 동안 인내심 있게 기다려야 한다) — give them time, Be patient, Express confidence의 핵심 요약
❌ ③ Taking away privileges is the fastest way to stop misbehavior.(특권 빼앗기가 잘못을 멈추는 가장 빠른 길) — 부모들이 이미 실패한 방식
❌ ④ Building a higher wall keeps children from repeating mistakes.(벽을 높이면 실수를 반복하지 않는다) — 글이 반박하는 유혹
det.tip: 요지 = 처벌 강화 대신 시간·인내·신뢰
